entries.reason: a preprocessor in front of an unsupervised estimator, over ColumnarTable and RowMatrix - the two types this package has. It adds no arithmetic: the fitted preprocessor travels WITH the model, so a prediction goes through the scaler the fit used, and the fit is the preprocessor fitted and applied, then the estimator fitted on its output. preprocessed(from:) answers the intermediate on its own, because a caller who wants to look at it needs a way to
entries.effect: the composed transformer: the fitted preprocessor and the estimator's fitted transformer
entries.source: the iOS 26.2 CreateMLComponents.swiftinterface for the declarations (PreprocessingEstimator, typealias Transformer = ComposedTransformer<Preprocessor, Estimator.Transformer>); the port's behaviour by tests/backports/host/createml/preprocessing, 17 checks

entries.reason: the same with a target column, and the one semantic that is genuinely different: the preprocessor is fitted over the FEATURES ONLY and the target column is put back untouched. Scaling a target is a different model - a tree's thresholds and a logistic regression's coefficients are both in the target's own units. The first version transformed the whole table, so the estimator saw a target whose mean was 0 and the test's `mean 17` came back `0.0`: the arithmetic was right and the column was the wrong one
entries.effect: the composed transformer, with the target in its own units
entries.source: the SDK's own interface; the target-column rule is the port's and its test pins both halves

entries.reason: the same pipeline where the inner estimator can be updated on new data. The one semantic the `Updatable` name changes: an update preprocesses the input BY the preprocessor the fit produced and touches the inner estimator only. Refitting the preprocessor would change the features the estimator was fitted on, which is a different model and not an update - and the test compares the preprocessor's statistics before and after an update to hold exactly that
entries.effect: the composed transformer, updated in place
entries.source: the SDK's own interface; the update's semantics are the port's and its test compares the statistics across one

entries.reason: the supervised and updatable pair, on the same terms: the target column out of the preprocessor's input and the inner estimator updated on what it produced
entries.effect: the composed transformer, updated in place, with the target in its own units
entries.source: the SDK's own interface; checked by tests/backports/host/createml/preprocessing

entries.reason: the fitted half of a pipeline: the preprocessor and the estimator's FITTED transformer (`Base.Transformer`, not `Base` - carrying the unfitted estimator would be carrying the thing the fit replaces). The two are left to the caller to join, because the framework's Transformer and TabularTransformer are different protocols with different input types and one composition cannot name both without erasing the pair
entries.effect: the two halves, and nothing joined
